schema.title: Response List Ssh Host Aliases Api Remote Servers Aliases Get

post.description:
Append a new Host entry to the user's ``~/.ssh/config`` and return it as a selectable alias.

For a user who wants to point Studio at a host without hand-editing their
SSH config first. Verifies the new host is actually reachable before
returning: a failed verification removes the entry it just wrote rather
than leaving an unreachable entry in the user's real config. Also rejects
an alias that already exists rather than editing it - see
`services.ssh_config_writer` for why.

``accepted_host_key_fingerprint`` mirrors the same header on remote-trainer
create/update: a genuinely new host has no ``known_hosts`` entry yet, so the
first attempt raises `exceptions.SshHostKeyUnknownError` and the caller
re-submits once the user confirms the fingerprint it surfaced.

get.description:

active.

Phase 1: Create a dataset import job immediately, before the archive is uploaded.

Returns a Job with step=awaiting_archive_upload. Use the returned job_id in the phase-2
upload endpoint to attach the archive and queue processing.

Phase 2: Upload the archive and attach it to an existing import job.

The job must be in the awaiting_archive_upload step (created via POST /datasets:prepare).
After this call the job transitions to step=queued_for_detection and status=pending so the
worker can pick it up for processing.

image_key_reorder_map.description: Camera name -> camera slot index, for a policy pretrained on a fixed camera order (SmolVLA). Empty keeps the dataset's own camera order. When set it must cover every camera the dataset has, since the policy matches it against the batch's image keys.

User-editable connection, image-pull, and shared-memory settings for SSH trainers.

SSH config, known-hosts paths, and the image registry remain environment-only.
Managed SSH access requires a loopback-bound Studio backend because the
settings API has no authentication model.

StatusMessage.title: StatusMessage
StatusMessage.description:
A part of the session or one of its devices saying how it is, on ``evt/status/<component>``.

``component`` is a path: ``environment``, ``control`` and ``dataset`` are the
session's parts, ``environment/follower``, ``environment/leader`` and
``environment/<camera key>`` the environment's devices. Devices report only
``starting``, ``running`` and ``failed``: a part that starts or stops takes its
devices with it, so their earlier statuses no longer apply.
